statements.finder_note: Restatement of a recurring call ('I often explain'). No date.

The author says their record of funding bad mental-health ideas (he cites Done) has shrunk the pool of clinicians who can build better care models and are willing to work with them; the group he speaks for will refuse to work with such investors.
statements.post_title: "Why Isn't Someone Already Doing This?"

statements.context: Step in an illustrative back-of-envelope count of how many US psychiatrists could lead tech-enabled, value-based mental health companies. From about 331 candidates the author removes those who will retire soon, citing AMA Insurance Agency survey data, leaving about 200. 'May' is a typo for 'Many' in the original.
statements.post_title: "Why Isn't Someone Already Doing This?"
statements.finder_note: Demographic extrapolation inside a calculation the author calls 'not a serious article when it comes to math'.

statements.context: End of the illustrative funnel: from 56,536 US psychiatrists, through TMS and ketamine practitioners, research authorship, in-network status, retirement, Y Combinator acceptance and startup failure rates, the author estimates that roughly 2.5 physician-led companies could become billion-dollar companies. He states up front that the math is not serious and he is making a point.
statements.post_title: "Why Isn't Someone Already Doing This?"
statements.finder_note: Illustrative numeric estimate; author says 'It's not a serious article when it comes to math—I'm making a point.' The number is rhetorical; the direction (very few) is sincere.
